title: Revisiting India’s first general election, 1951–52
shows: The Hindu's visual story retells India's first general election, which began in Chini and Pangi in Himachal Pradesh on 25 October 1951 and ran until February 1952. By the paper's account, provincial and State governments were asked in November 1947 to plan the preparation of electoral rolls, compiling began in November 1950, Bihar, Orissa and Punjab were among the last to publish preliminary rolls in March 1951, and the final rolls were published in November 1951. It puts those eligible to vote at around 17.3 crore and those who voted at 10.6 crore, and says around 28 lakh entries for women listed only as someone's wife or mother were deleted because the Commission insisted that women be registered in their own names. It also covers Sukumar Sen, the first Chief Election Commissioner, Shyam Saran Negi, remembered as the first voter, the separate ballot box for each candidate, the results and the closest contests.
quote: The process of compiling electoral rolls began in November 1950, with Bihar, Orissa, and Punjab among the last States to publish preliminary rolls, in March 1951. After corrections and additions, the final electoral rolls were published in November 1951.
As many women had been listed only through their relationships with male family members, around 28 lakh entries were struck off from the list.
